To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The hydrated autoclaving immunohistochemical procedure for detection of scrapie-associated PrP in formalin-fixed brain tissue was adapted to automated capillary electrophoresis flow technology; 2) The automated capillary electroporesis flow procedure was more sensitive for detection of scrapic-associated PrP than the conventional immunohistochemistry procedure, with 10% of the sample required for the automated method compared to 100% of the sample for the conventional method;

(1) the hydrated autoclave IHC method is applicable to formalinfixed sheep brain; (2) the method is sensitive and specific; (3) the method is suitable for use in automated capillary flow IHC instruments; (4) the method is useful for the diagnosis of scrapie in sheep; and (5) the method can be used to detect PrP-res in sheep brain with a sensitivity and accuracy similar to those achieved with the Western blot method.

the use of a 3,3-diaminobenzidine substrate for detection of PrP-res by IHC in formalin-fixed, paraffinembedded tissues is a rapid, simple method that is suitable for use in large scale diagnostic surveys for sheep scrapie.
